project_comments.note: Architecture observation spanning WP-001 and WP-002: all three LedgerStore write methods (updateWorkPackageWithSync, createWorkPackageWithSync, batchUpdateWorkPackagesWithSync) guarantee lock-scoped atomicity — no concurrent writer can observe a partial state. However, none of them provide rollback-across-multiple-files semantics: if atomicWriteJson succeeds for WP-001 and then fails (or Zod rejects) for WP-002, WP-001 remains written on disk. This is an inherent property of the file-per-entity storage model and matches the existing pre-refactor behavior. Future work should document this contract explicitly in the LedgerStore class JSDoc ('lock-scoped, not transaction-scoped') so new contributors do not assume ACID rollback guarantees."

ARCHITECTURAL INVARIANT — batchUpdateWorkPackagesWithSync validate-all-then-write-all: The original implementation of batchUpdateWorkPackagesWithSync interleaved validation and disk writes in a single loop (validate WP then write WP, repeat). This meant a Zod validation failure on WP-N could leave WP-1 through WP-(N-1) already written to disk while the root index remained in the pre-batch state — the WP-file/root-index desync bug that the entire consolidate-wp-writes project exists to prevent. Fixed in code review by splitting into two passes: Pass 1 validates all WPs and the root index, collecting pre-validated WorkPackageDetail objects; Pass 2 writes all pre-validated objects to disk. Any failure in Pass 1 aborts before any file is touched. A new test ('mid-batch validation failure') was added to ledger-store.test.ts to document and protect this guarantee. Future changes to batchUpdateWorkPackagesWithSync must preserve the two-pass structure. See commit on feature-extended-workflow branch, mcp-server/src/storage/ledger-store.ts lines 349-365.
